context.in_practice: Text with several lines is shown as indented lines. A marker on the first line records whether the text ends in a newline, has no final newline (`|-`) or keeps extra blank lines at the end (`|+`). Trailing spaces, tabs and a leading blank line are kept. Text with Windows line endings (\r) or control characters stays in one double-quoted line with escapes. The arms on route 1 split only on text whose first line starts with spaces: five show it as lines, using the `|2` indent marker, and one keeps it double-quoted.
context.stakes: When a setting holds text that spans several lines, such as a prompt, `config show` decides whether you see it as readable lines or as one escaped string. It also decides whether that text survives being copied back into the file without changes like lost trailing newlines, stripped spaces or altered line endings.
context.tradeoff: Route 1: most multi-line text is easy to read and copies back exactly, but you have to read markers like `|-`, `|+` and `|2`, and text with \r or control characters still appears as an escaped one-liner.

plan_why: Runs `show` on sections that hold non-include multi-line strings of several shapes. This shows how each one is printed: as a literal block (|, |-, |+, or with an indentation indicator) or as a double-quoted scalar when a block can't hold it exactly (CR, control characters, blank-padded lines).
routes: Literal block when it can hold them exactly, else double-quoted
